newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends up slightly in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends up slightly in thin dealings.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended barely firmer in light activity as prices consolidated Friday's sharp gains, market sources said.
"We had a lot of activity last week but there is no news," said Sharon Johnson, analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc.
Cold wet weather across the cotton belt may be providing support for new-crop futures, market sources said.
Near term, players await Tuesday's spec/hedge report but little change is expected from last week as the speculators continue to hold a large net short position.
Shortcovering is expected to lift most-active July to 74.00 and then to 75.00 cents a lb, analysts said.
July delivery ended 0.04 cent firmer at 73.53 cents, traded 73.70 to 73.20 cents. New-crop December finished up 0.19 at 75.96 cents.
Volume was estimated at 4,500 lots compared with Friday's official 7,779 lots.
Certificated stocks as of April 25 were unchanged from the previous session at 220,870 480-lb bales.
Open interest in May stood at 603 lots, down 410 lots as of early Friday. Interest in July eased by 241 lots to 41,689 lots.
